Due to a lack of reference values and model access, H0-mini [ 23 ] could not be compared on each robustness benchmark. A comparison to H0-mini [ 23 ] on published results shows that for the CLS+MEAN representation the average robustness on PathoROB [ 46 ] is 7.2 p.p. better for Atlas 2-B (88.7 vs. 81.5). On the CLS token evaluation for Plismbench [ 22 ] , Atlas 2-B outperforms H0-mini by nearly 10 p.p. (63.9 vs. 54.1). For clinical deployment, foundation models must demonstrate both high prediction performance for the task at hand and robustness to confounding data variations commonly seen in routine diagnostics. Additionally, the large volume of histological slides produced in pathology labs necessitates efficient processing to provide timely and cost-effective analyses. Our novel pathology foundation models Atlas 2, as well as its efficient, distilled versions 2-B and 2-S were trained on the to date largest dataset used for pathology foundation model development comprising 5.5 million histological slides. Our models show consistent state of the art performance on all three important requirements — prediction performance, robustness, and resource efficiency. The evaluation was performed on eighty benchmarks from five different public benchmark suits covering a wide variety of tasks, datasets, and tissue types.
